title: Oversized or too-deeply-nested SQL is silently half-parsed instead of rejected
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

sqlparse has limits on grouping depth and on the number of tokens in a token list (meant to protect against DoS). When input exceeds them, the library quietly gives up on grouping and returns a poorly processed result with no indication anything went wrong. It should instead raise `sqlparse.exceptions.SQLParseError`.

Example 1:
    import sqlparse
    sql = "SELECT " + "(" * 200 + "1" + ")" * 200
    sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True)
EXPECTED: raises SQLParseError whose message contains "Maximum grouping depth exceeded".
ACTUAL: returns a formatted string (408 chars), no error.

Example 2:
    sql = "SELECT " + ", ".join(f"col{i}" for i in range(15000)) + " FROM table1"
    sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True)
EXPECTED: raises SQLParseError whose message contains "Maximum number of tokens exceeded".
ACTUAL: returns a ~139k char string, no error.

Same rule for a huge tuple list, e.g. `WHERE (a, b) IN ((1, 1), (1, 2), ... 5000 tuples)` formatted with reindent=True and keyword_case="upper": it should raise SQLParseError with "Maximum number of tokens exceeded". Normal-sized SQL (including ~100 tuples) must keep working unchanged.
acceptance: Excessive nesting depth raises SQLParseError with a message containing "Maximum grouping depth exceeded"
Token lists over the limit (long column list, 5000-tuple IN list) raise SQLParseError with a message containing "Maximum number of tokens exceeded"
Ordinary queries and a 100-tuple IN list still format normally
